name: a-packed-unorm-pair-picks-the-row-the-shader-reads
rationale:
venueWallShadow_vertex packs a vertex attribute into a normalized 16-bit pair, takes the low half as an index, and reads two arrays with it. The index is the whole case: the observed varying is the float4 the shader read at that index, so a packing that lands one row away returns a completely different colour rather than a slightly different number. Nothing here is approximate -- air.pack.unorm2x16.v2f32 is round(saturate(x) * 65535), an integer, and the value it produces is used as an integer.

Eight triangles, one per pixel of an 8x1 target, each carrying the same attribute at all three of its vertices so the interpolated varying is exact and no answer depends on a barycentric weight. Each triangle's base is a fifth of a pixel wide and narrows to a point, so at the row of pixel centres it covers its own centre and comes nowhere near its neighbours'. The eight attributes are chosen at (k - 0.4)/65535: multiplying by 65535 lands four tenths below a whole number, so ROUNDING reaches k and TRUNCATING reaches k-1, and every one of the eight would read the wrong row if the round were dropped. The indices run 1 through 7 and then 15, which is the last row of the sixteen, so an off-by-one at the top of the array shows up as well as one at the bottom. The sixteen colours are distinct and exactly representable, so no row can be mistaken for another.

The rest of the shader is arranged to stay out of the way. Every direction entry is zero, so the unpacked second attribute multiplies to nothing and the clip position is the position attribute unchanged; the view matrix is the identity, so the three column loads and the two multiply-adds reproduce it exactly rather than transforming it. That leaves the packed index as the only thing the observation can be reading.

name: custom-filter-passthrough-zero-state-variant
rationale: A zero shader-state vector disables every optional texture, table, framebuffer-fetch, and dithering branch. The separately linked visible callback returns its incoming half4 unchanged, while zeroed mandatory globals and custom arguments keep every reachable access in bounds. The poisoned one-pixel half4 render target observes the exact linked fragment result.

name: linked-zero-destination-vector-lut-dequantize-4bit-unaligned
rationale: A single invocation computes coordinate zero while the authored destination extent is zero in every dimension. The top-level destination bounds guard returns before any source, LUT, destination, loop, or linked-function access, leaving the sole poisoned output unchanged.

name: reset-specular-indirect-count
rationale: The loop-free entry ignores its grid index and unconditionally replaces the complete poisoned four-byte indirect-specular entry counter with aligned i32 zero.

name: vertex-float2-position-with-buffer-depth
rationale: Three authored float2 positions form a full-coverage triangle; constant buffer slot 1 supplies finite clip-space depth 0.25, and the typed position observer captures the structural expansion to (x, y, depth, 1).

name: linked-single-fft-temp-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded FFT work item with unit extents and strides. The destination-temp path confines writes to the authored output allocation. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert. The authored threadgroup allocation bounds the combined-radix scratch footprint.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-seven-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 7 and receives exact float4 zero from all six linked _uber_clear bodies. A nine-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before subgroup aggregation, and binding zero is captured byte-exactly.

name: linked-single-threadgroup-zero-bin
rationale: One 1x1 threadgroup dispatches one invocation. kLogBinEntries=0 makes both initialization and flush loops contain exactly one bin, kTGSizeIs256=false uses the literal one-thread group size as their stride, and source_size=1x1 bounds the image path. The exact linked callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing resources; the poisoned global bin makes the local-atomic aggregation observable byte-exactly.

name: widen-a-range-by-three-and-a-half-without-contracting
rationale: The module is compiled air.compile.fast_math_disable, so its `avg + d*3.5` and `avg - d*3.5` are a separate multiply and add that Metal must not fuse. An average above the maximum makes the half-extent negative, which is what keeps the two fmin/fmax clamps from masking either result, and the very low minimum keeps the other clamp open. The three inputs are chosen so that the rounded product differs from the exact one and both the widened lower and upper bound land on a different float when the pair is contracted into an fma, so the observed 68 bytes distinguish contraction from its absence.

name: constant-half4-white
rationale: The fragment entry ignores its stage inputs and returns literal half4 (1,1,1,1) at color location zero; one full-coverage fragment must replace the complete poisoned pixel.

name: resample-one-texel-centre-from-the-second-source-layer
rationale: A 2x4 dispatch; the observed texel is the invocation at tid (1, 3, 0). destinationSize is (2, 4, 1), so no lane of the `any(destinationSize <= tid)` guard fires for any invocation and all eight run. air.convert.f.v3f32.u.v3i16 turns that tid into (1.0, 3.0, 0.0) -- the two non-zero lanes differ, so a conversion that swaps lanes, narrows, or drops one moves the sample. scaleFactor is (1/8, 1/8), so the coordinate is (1/8 + 1/2, 3/8 + 1/2) = (0.625, 0.875), and on a four-wide four-tall source those are exactly the centres of texels 2 and 3: every term is a dyadic rational, so the multiply-add is exact and the sample is unambiguous for any filter. The sampler is authored nearest anyway. sourceOrigin is (0, 0, 1), so the signed conversion feeding the layer picks source layer 1, and air.convert.u.i32.f.f32 truncates 1.0 to slice 1. The 32 source texels are all distinct, so landing on the wrong texel, the wrong layer, or the wrong destination texel changes the bytes; the answer is source layer 1 texel (2, 3), which is (132, 132.25, 132.5, 132.75). What this case cannot separate is unsigned from signed on the tid conversion, because a thread position is never negative.

name: blit-through-a-uniform-rasterization-rate-map
rationale: Metal ground truth for air.map_screen_to_physical_coordinates.v2f32.p2i8.i32 (34 case-less sources). The translator lowers it to the identity, which is correct only for a rasterization rate map whose rate is a uniform 1.0, and until now nothing pinned that. Buffer 0 carries the real parameter data of such a map -- a 64x64 screen, one layer, all-1.0 horizontal and vertical rates, produced by MTLRasterizationRateMap.copyParameterData, whose physicalSize equals its screenSize. Our reflection reports that buffer Unused because the identity model never reads it, so the Metal side decodes real map data and the Vulkan side does not: the two agree only if the identity is the right answer. The static sampler is pixel-coordinate ClampToEdge LINEAR, so sampling at float2(gid) puts the filter weight at exactly one half on every axis, and the source texel (x, y, x+y, 1) makes every blend a half-integer that is exact in binary32. The offset buffer is zero, so the destination coordinate is the thread id and a mapping that scaled or shifted the sample coordinate would move every texel.

name: put-the-ninetieth-percentile-exactly-on-a-bin-edge
rationale: A 90th-percentile search whose two-stage scan is built from air.simd_prefix_inclusive_sum.u.i32: each of the eight simdgroups scans its own 32 histogram bins, then simdgroup 0 walks the seven block boundaries in lockstep to turn the per-simdgroup scans into one 256-bin prefix sum. One 256-thread threadgroup makes threads_per_simdgroup=32 and simdgroups_per_threadgroup=8, so every stride loop runs exactly once and all three threadgroup barriers stay convergent. linearSystemStatus=0 takes the working path instead of the early store of zero. The counts are chosen so the whole float tail is exact rather than merely close: the total is 2^23, the only total for which 0.9f times it is an integer (0.9f = 15099494*2^-24, so the product needs 2^23 to clear the odd factor), giving a threshold of exactly 7549747. Bins 100 and 200 hold 6710886 and 1677722, so the prefix crosses the threshold first at bin 200 with 6710886 below and 8388608 at it -- and (7549747-6710886)/(8388608-6710886) is exactly 1/2. At t=0.5 Metal's mix(x,y,a)=x+(y-x)a and GLSL's FMix=x(1-a)+ya agree bit-for-bit, so the case does not silently depend on which formula the lowering picks, and the fdiv is exact under a reciprocal-multiply as well. The result collapses to bin/32 = 6.25.
